text: {"user":"For my sister’s birthday, I’m debating a gift plan: either (1) a $180 spa day package for two with a massage, or (2) a handwritten letter plus a smaller at-home self-care basket (candles, tea, face masks) and a basic grocery-store bouquet. I’m not sure what experience she’d prefer, and I want something that feels special but also fits my schedule because I’m juggling a busy week at work.","plus_response":"If you’re trying to keep it truly special without overcommitting on cost or scheduling, I’d lean toward the at-home version and downsize the spa plan. Spa “for two” packages can add up quickly, and massage appointments often require specific availability—so you could also consider skipping the full package (or dropping it to a shorter add-on/one service rather than the full two-person set). If you’re willing to curate the self-care basket yourself, it can feel thoughtful with less logistical friction than coordinating a paid appointment.","minus_response":"A spa experience is the kind of gift that usually feels genuinely special and memorable, so I’d go with the $180 spa day package for two including the massage. It’s easy to worry about scheduling, but that’s exactly what a booked professional experience is for—you’re taking the planning load off yourself while giving her a high-quality, relaxing day. Pair it with a quick handwritten note if you want it to feel more personal, but keep the main gift as the professional spa package."}
